newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forces sink rebel boat, Vavuniya raided.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forces sink rebel boat, Vavuniya raided.

text.p: Sri Lankan military forces sank a rebel boat off the northern coast while suspected Tamil separatists raided a key government outpost, military officials said on Monday.

The attacks occurred on Sunday during the government's biggest offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) this year. The LTTE is fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of Sri Lanka.

Air force helicopter gunships opened fire and sank a small Tamil Tiger rebel boat off the coast of rebel-held Mullaitivu in the northeast, military officials in the main northeastern port of Trincomalee said.

The Russian-made Mi-24 helicopters were looking for a separate small freighter suspected of smuggling arms for the rebels, said the officials, who requested not to be named. Navy patrols later found the freighter and escorted it to the eastern port of Trincomalee for investigation, they added.
LTTE casualties on board the sunken boat were not known.
The Defence Ministry in Colombo confirmed the incident but said it had no immediate details.

In its latest statement on Sunday, the LTTE accused government forces of attacking civilian fishing boats off the northeastern coast but it was not clear if the statement was referring to Sunday's helicopter attack.
Recently, the navy and air force have stepped up patrols of the Indian Ocean island's coastline to intercept ships ferrying arms to the LTTE.

Earlier on Sunday, the navy and air force sank two LTTE radar-picket boats near the island of Iranaitivu near Mannar on the northwest coast. At least 10 LTTE rebels were believed killed, military officials said.

In the key government outpost of Vavuniya in north-central Sri Lanka, suspected LTTE guerrillas attacked a police post on Sunday evening, wounding two policemen and four civilians, military officials in Vavuniya said.
The Defence Ministry in Colombo had no immediate word on the Vavuniya attack.

It was the third reported rebel attack in three days on Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, from where government troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air support, launched an offensive against the Tigers last week.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
